items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: I went out with Larry Elgart and did a few, about a half year with him.

ctx.x: Why would you do that I guess. Is it harder to rise in the ranks of the classical world or in the jazz world?

The first thing I noticed, I did the classical world first. I was doing shows and I was doing symphony orchestras, I played with the Symphony of the Air and various, like I said, the American Opera Society and various groups before I really got into the commercial end of it, which came about through my having a spare weekend and I went out with Larry Elgart and did a few, about a half year with him. And it segued into Gerry Mulligan with

the concert jazz band. I found on the way up that jazz musicians had ears. They could hear way beyond the instrument. And I found out at the same time, of course people are going to raise eyebrows at this, that classical musicians, although some of them have wonderful ears, by and large they are pretty much into their instrument. A clarinet player hears the world in relation to the clarinet. And this is a generalization but this is what I found at that time, and we are talking mid and late 50s and early 60s. The…
